notes: Focal pathogen. Major pre- and post-harvest fungal pathogen of peanut (Arachis hypogaea) and maize, causing yellow mold disease and producing carcinogenic aflatoxins; extensive literature on A. flavus-peanut molecular interactions (e.g. Jayaprakash et al. 2023, J Proteom 287:104975). Genome/proteome fully sequenced (Nierman et al. 2015, Genome Announc). This system has NOT been analyzed by the mimicDetector paper (which surveyed 17 pathogens targeting the human proteome only), so this is a genuinely new application of the pipeline.
Host plant (cultivated peanut); allotetraploid (AABB genome, A. duranensis x A. ipaensis), reference genome/annotation from Bertioli et al. 2019, Nat Genet 51:877-884.

Domesticated, industrially used ("koji mold") close relative of A. flavus, long used in food fermentation (sake, soy sauce, miso) and NOT a plant pathogen. Reported ~99.5% gene homology to A. flavus NRRL3357 (PMC3901201), and widely discussed as an apparently domesticated, non-toxigenic, non-pathogenic derivative-or-sister lineage of A. flavus. This satisfies mimicDetector's own stated control-selection guidance ("appropriate controls include species that are more closely related to the pathogen than to the host") about as closely as any real, available proteome could. FLAGGED LIMITATION: because A. oryzae is SO close to A. flavus, this control is expected to be unusually stringent (most A. flavus k-mers will also match A. oryzae well), likely reducing the number of surviving candidates relative to a more distantly related control. A less stringent secondary/sensitivity-check control was considered but not run in this analysis, due to the computational cost of repeating the structural (POPScomp) stage against a new control species.
